_readme: Machine-readable map of the Phase 1 provider fixtures to the downstream behaviour they exist to test. Owned by integrations-engineer; pipeline/scoring/drafting/verification tests should key off this rather than hard-coding fixture names. tests/test_adapters.py asserts this file stays consistent with what is actually on disk.

expected.notes: Careers page carries a Revenue Operations Manager req plus two SDR openings - roles a B2B SaaS revenue product directly supports. Must score above threshold. Also the two-leads-one-domain case: enriching both leads must produce ONE research_cache row and ONE company-adapter call (assert adapter.call_count == 1).
Funding news only. The brief calls funding nearly worthless because every competitor's tool leads with it. Nothing may clear the threshold and no generic draft may be forced.

expected.unverifiable_claim_example: now that you've scaled to 40 support reps
expected.notes: Material is real but vague: one support req and a 'the team has grown a lot' post, with no numbers anywhere. A draft asserting a specific headcount cites nothing and verification must fail closed.
Successful lookup, nothing found. A valid route to no_angle.
No fixture file on purpose. Models a dead URL / dead domain: still a successful lookup, so also a valid route to no_angle.
The adapter raises after bounded retries. This must NEVER reach no_angle: a swallowed provider error would forge the 'we found nothing' verdict the client acts on.
